references.text: The prophecy that the dead will wake up and live, as a direct parallel to Jesus' statement that the dead will hear and live.
God's promise to open the graves and give life to the dead, so that they may hear God's voice and receive life.
The prophet is commanded to call out to the dead, so that they may hear the Lord's voice and receive life, an image fulfilled by Jesus.
Jesus calls with a loud voice to the dead Lazarus, who hears and comes out of the grave, a concrete fulfillment of the principle in this verse.
Jesus explains that no one can come to him unless the Father draws them, and that those who hear and learn from the Father come to him, connected to the listening that gives life.
Jesus identifies himself as the resurrection and the life, promising that whoever believes in him will live even if they die, a direct extension of the theme of the dead hearing and living.
